design:
Where it lives (operator, 2026-11-04): a new project tab, Checkpoints, beside Thread/Tasks/Spec/Vault/Jobs/Activity. A conversation's menu and an agent's screen open it already narrowed. The existing per-conversation modal is replaced by the tab, not kept beside it. The view is built first as real components fed fixtures (hub/ui/mock), and the operator judges that mock before the build is approved.

Title and summary come from the same generation call as the rest of the checkpoint (operator, 2026-11-02). They are required parts of its answer; an over-long one is a rejection, not cut short. A rejected answer is asked for once more, naming what was wrong. After a second rejection, the Hub makes the title from the body's first words and marks it as made by the Hub.

When neither answer can be read at all (no readable structure, or the model could not be reached), there are no first words to use (operator, 2026-11-04). The title is then made from what the Hub knows (agent, trigger and date), the checkpoint keeps the files, tasks, questions and citations the Hub recorded itself, and whatever raw text the model returned is kept behind a 'show what the model returned' link, never shown as the body.

Hazard (Tier 2): this adds stored fields to checkpoints (a migration), and the one-time fill runs on its own against the operator's real data at their next restart, spending model tokens (about 100k on a cheap model for 75 checkpoints). Rollback: the migration's downgrade drops the new fields, and the view falls back to showing the trigger and date where a title is missing. The fill is resumable: a checkpoint already given a title is never sent again, and one failure does not stop the others.

lifecycle:
A checkpoint's title and summary are in one of four states:
- written: the model wrote them, and the first or second answer was accepted.
- made from the body: both answers were rejected, so the title and summary come from the body's first words and opening sentences, marked as made by the Hub, with the rejection reason.
- made from the Hub's facts: neither answer could be read, so the title is made from the agent, trigger and date, marked as made by the Hub, with any raw text kept behind a link.
- awaiting the fill: an older checkpoint the one-time fill has not reached yet. A checkpoint whose fill could not reach the model returns to this state and is tried again at the next start.
Nothing moves a checkpoint out of written or either made-by-the-Hub state.

open_questions.question: When neither answer can be read at all. Operator 2026-11-04: title from agent, trigger and date; keep the Hub-recorded files, tasks, questions and citations; raw text behind a 'show what the model returned' link, never as the body.
Where the checkpoints view lives. Operator 2026-11-04: a new project tab, judged in the mock.
Second rejection. Operator 2026-11-02: fall back to the checkpoint's first words; never leave a checkpoint with no information.
A rejected answer. Operator 2026-11-02: ask the model once more before giving up.
When the one-time fill runs. Operator 2026-11-02: on its own in the background at the first start after this change.
Output missing the title. Operator 2026-11-02: the title is obligatory; output without it is rejected.
Limits. Operator 2026-11-02: title at most 8 words and 60 characters, summary at most two sentences and 300 characters; going over is a rejection, not cut short.
Who fills the existing checkpoints. Operator 2026-11-02: the Hub runs a one-time pass; no agent tool.
Older checkpoints: fallback or fill. Operator 2026-11-02: fill them once.

problem: Checkpoints are generated well (75 on the operator's Hub on 2026-11-02, 73 passed their probe), but the operator's reading is that the checkpoint screen 'doesn't show anything useful' and may not work. The only view is a modal opened from a conversation's overflow menu (ConversationBar.tsx:196), and it lists only that conversation's checkpoints (hub/hub/api/v1/checkpoints.py:88). The 75 checkpoints are spread across 74 conversations, so it rarely shows more than one. A conversation started by a cut-over (18 so far) shows 'No checkpoint has been taken', because the checkpoint it was born from stays on the predecessor. The body is shown as raw markdown in a monospace block (CheckpointsPanel.tsx:61). Status, trigger and probe are shown in internal words ('ready', 'task completion', 'Probe: passed'). Nothing says which runs a checkpoint covers, and nothing tells checkpoints apart without opening each one: the generation writes objective, state, decisions, dead ends, next actions and risks (checkpoint_generation.py:73-95), but no title or summary.

requirements.rationale: Today the only list is scoped to one conversation, and 75 checkpoints sit in 74 conversations, so the list almost never shows more than one.
requirements.statement: The project has a checkpoints view that lists every checkpoint the project holds, newest first, across all agents and conversations, including checkpoints whose conversation is archived or was carried over.
Each listed checkpoint shows its title, summary, the agent that produced it, what triggered it, when it was taken, its status, and the conversation it belongs to.

requirements.rationale: The operator defined a checkpoint's type as what triggered it (2026-11-02); the type only helps if it can be read.
requirements.statement: A checkpoint's trigger and status are shown in words that describe what happened (for example that a task finished, that the operator asked, that the conversation grew long), not the Hub's internal identifiers such as 'task_completion' or 'probe passed'.
The checkpoints view can be narrowed to one agent, to one trigger, and to one conversation, and the narrowing can be combined.
From a conversation, and from an agent, the operator reaches the checkpoints view already narrowed to that conversation or that agent.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: every screen a checkpoint can be reached from is to be checked, and each should open the right one.
requirements.statement: Every screen that mentions a specific checkpoint (including the offer to carry a conversation over, and the notice that a checkpoint is being written or is ready) opens that checkpoint, not a list it has to be found in.
An opened checkpoint renders its body as formatted text (headings, lists, emphasis), not as markdown source.
An opened checkpoint names the runs it covers, and each named run opens that run's trace.
An opened checkpoint shows the files changed, the open questions, the citations, and the agent notes it carried, each only when present.

A checkpoint that failed, or whose title was made by the Hub, is listed like any other and, when opened, says why: the reason its answers were rejected or could not be read, or what its probe found missing or invented.

requirements.rationale: Today the successor shows 'No checkpoint has been taken in this conversation' (18 such conversations on 2026-11-02), which is the likeliest reason the screen reads as broken.
requirements.statement: A conversation started by carrying over a checkpoint shows that checkpoint as the one it started from, and the conversation it was carried from shows which conversation it was carried into.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: the checkpoint generation is already a manager-like run, so it is asked for this data rather than a separate distillation pass being added. Length agreed the same day.
requirements.statement: Every checkpoint generated after this change carries a title of at most 8 words and 60 characters and a summary of at most two sentences and 300 characters, written by the same model call that writes the rest of its body; no separate model call is made to write them.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: the title is obligatory, an over-long one is rejected rather than shortened, a rejected answer is asked for once more, and a checkpoint must never end with no information. Operator, 2026-11-04: an answer that cannot be read at all is titled from the Hub's facts, and its raw text is kept behind a link rather than shown as the body, so junk never reads as a summary. Today any rejected answer loses the whole written body with no retry (hub/hub/worker.py:579-589).
requirements.statement: The Hub accepts a checkpoint generation's answer only when it includes a title and a summary within those limits. When an answer is rejected, the Hub asks the model once more, saying what was wrong. When the second answer is rejected too, the checkpoint is still saved with every part of the answer that could be read, a title made from the first words of its body, a summary made from its opening sentences, a mark that they were made by the Hub rather than written by the model, and the reason the answers were rejected. When neither answer can be read at all, the title is made from the agent, the trigger and the date, the checkpoint keeps the files, tasks, questions and citations the Hub recorded, it is marked as made by the Hub with the reason, and any raw text the model returned is available on request but is not shown as the body.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: fill the existing checkpoints in one go rather than show a fallback, have the Hub do it rather than an agent, and run it on its own at the first start. All 75 existing checkpoints have a body (387,653 characters in total, about 100k tokens on a cheap model).
requirements.statement: Every checkpoint that existed before this change is given a title and summary within the same limits once, by a pass the Hub runs on its own in the background after its first start on this change, reading only that checkpoint's existing body, so that no checkpoint in the view is left without them; the same ask-once-more and first-words fallback applies.

in_scope: A project-level Checkpoints tab listing every checkpoint across agents and conversations, including archived and carried-over conversations.
Reaching that view narrowed to one conversation or one agent from where that conversation or agent is shown.
Every screen that mentions a specific checkpoint opening that checkpoint.
Each checkpoint's title, summary, agent, trigger, date, status and conversation in the list.
An opened checkpoint: its body rendered as formatted text, the runs it covers, files changed, open questions, citations, the agent notes it carried, and why it failed when it did.
A carried-over conversation showing the checkpoint it started from, and its predecessor showing where it was carried to.

The checkpoint generation writing a title and summary as required parts of the same model call, asked once more when its answer is rejected, and falling back to the checkpoint's first words, or to the Hub's facts when no answer can be read.
Giving the checkpoints that already exist a title and summary, once, by a pass the Hub runs on its own after it starts.
non_goals: Starting a conversation from a checkpoint (slice 'start-from-a-checkpoint').
Any new trace screen (slices 'traces-you-can-browse', 'conversation-trace', 'woven-traces'); a covered run opens the run trace the app already has.
A separate distillation or manager run over checkpoints as an ongoing process (operator, 2026-11-02: the checkpoint is already that run). The one-time fill of existing checkpoints is not ongoing.
An agent tool that writes a checkpoint's title or summary (operator, 2026-11-02: the Hub runs the one-time fill).
How checkpoints are probed, and when they are triggered.
Varying the generation prompt by trigger.

summary: A slice of 'Checkpoints and traces you can find and use'. A new Checkpoints project tab lists every checkpoint in the project. Each one can be told apart at a glance by its title and summary, its agent, its trigger and its date, and opens as readable text that names the runs it covers. A conversation carried over from a checkpoint shows the checkpoint it started from, and every screen that mentions a checkpoint opens it. Taken off the shelf on 2026-11-04, after the operator settled its last two questions; built in parallel with checks roadmap slice 3.
